P1.evidence: Setter notes were used conversationally rather than read back — 'he told me you had a really bad motorcycle accident', 'I think you had six surgeries, was it?', 'you're a tattoo artist, right?' — which is warmer than nothing but is not the structured playback the script asks for. Frame two-part: 'I just want to get probably a better idea than what Kim got of kind of where you're at now and where you want to be... And then if I feel like we can help, I can walk you through all of this stuff.' No agreement was sought at all. Open question run.

P2.evidence: By a wide margin the most thorough baseline in the batch. Age asked directly ('How old are you, by the way?'), work established and probed ('What prevented you from going back?'), health history run properly ('Are you fully recovered? I think you had six surgeries, was it? You recovered in terms of post-surgery rehab done?'), and the injury question run to a genuine site-by-site map across two questions — 'are there still areas of like pain and discomfort?' followed by 'and do you have pain when you're not working out?'. Training week, results from that training and diet all elicited cleanly. Height, weight, sleep and energy are the only gaps. The point for the audit is that the information was gathered comprehensively and then not acted on: this rep knew about the brain surgery, the tremors, the four pain sites and the prematurely stopped rehab before he presented anything.

P3.evidence: The strongest goals work in the batch. 'When you say function normal and normal life, what are some things that you can't do at the moment?' produced running, jumping and crouching to tie a shoe. 'If we were to fast forward six months, what's really the outcome you're looking for?' and then 'imagine in six months' time you're back where you want to be playing basketball, going on runs — what would that be like for you?' reached the real answer: 'I would just be a lot happier, a lot less stress on my plate because I'd be able to get out, clear my mind.' The livelihood link was drawn too. What is missing is 'who else does that impact' and any reflect-back — nobody said 'so this isn't really about the body, it's about getting your life back'.

P4.evidence: 'What kind of progress have you seen over the last six months?' surfaced the real problem — six months of training five days a week with almost nothing to show for it — and the prospect named both gaps himself: 'I think a lot of that also is my diet' and 'I don't have much structure in my workouts that I'm doing now. I just go in and do things and I don't have no plan.' The history of what stopped (physical therapy ended for financial reasons) was established. Not asked: why he thinks the last six months produced so little, what the single thing in the way is, or the root-cause line.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame ran. Recorded as a miss because the phase was reachable and not run, but flagged for the coach as the one call in this batch where skipping it was arguably right — asking a 24-year-old eleven months out from a near-fatal collision what two more years of this looks like would have been gratuitous, and his cost of inaction was already the entire content of the call.

P6.evidence: The belief question was never asked. 'Is there anything that you feel like is missing in terms of the process that you feel like you need?' is a weak stand-in for the all-in check and it came after the presentation. Most importantly P6c was breached: the prospect's answer to affordability was hesitation — 'It would definitely be hard for me to do... it's going to be hard for me financially' — and the playbook says to return to Phase 5 on hesitation. Instead the rep continued to the close and then reduced the entry payment until the hesitation was engineered away. Credit where due on sequencing: he did quote the price before the pitch, explicitly to avoid exciting someone who could not afford it, which is better practice than anywhere else in the batch.

P11.evidence: Payment reached the link stage at a $1,200 minimum with the balance pending a crypto sale; the recording stops before anything is confirmed. Onboarding was agreed for Monday in principle but no time was fixed — the rep started to pull up the calendar and the connection dropped. No agreement email, nothing signed on the call, no welcome email, no Skool link, no questionnaire — which matters more than usual here given the prospect volunteered significant memory impairment and will be relying on written follow-up.

objection_plays.detail: The most financial-picture work anywhere in this batch, and still only one item of the block. The rep pre-empted the objection honestly, offered the split, and then asked the cash question directly — 'How much do you have available, like cash on hand?' — which is FINANCIAL PICTURE item one. Crypto surfaced from the prospect rather than from the investments question. Not run: the ISOLATE ('finances aside, nothing else keeping you from 100%?'), the HOW-not-SHOULD frame, the permission question, and everything on cards, available credit and monthly surplus. And the play was used in an unusual direction — not to open a wallet but to find the smallest number that would still book the call, landing on $1,200 after the prospect offered $500.
No request for time; the prospect was ready throughout.
No third party in the decision.
Timing was not raised as an obstacle — the only timing question was whether payment had to be made today.

No fear or doubt about the programme. The prospect's only expressed doubt was about himself: 'if there's ever times where I'm asking you guys the same question over again, I apologize for that. I have pretty bad memory now from this accident.'

The clinical script gap at its most acute. Every screening trigger the playbook does not contain was present at once: brain surgery, unresolved neurological symptoms under active investigation, four sites of load-provoked pain, an inability to run or jump, a stated fear of re-fracturing, and rehabilitation abandoned mid-course for financial reasons. There is no scripted stop, no clearance question and no disqualification path, so the rep improvised in the only direction the script points — he converted the clinical picture into a reason to buy, telling the prospect the core work would mean his knees, ankles and back would stop hurting and that 'everything's healing in the correct way'. A second, related gap: no play exists for a prospect who is financially vulnerable enough that the purchase competes with medical care he has already had to stop.

notes: Technically the best discovery in the batch — a thorough baseline, the strongest goals work, a genuine cash-on-hand question and an honest early price check — and the call that should most clearly not have closed. He established brain surgery, live tremors, memory loss, four pain sites and abandoned rehab, then promised the pain would stop and reduced the entry payment to $1,200 to get it booked. The coaching point is not a technique: it is that the process has no stop, and this rep would have used one if it existed.
